summary: Game Crashes when Shift Command Delete 18 characters at once on Anvil

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft 1.14.3.  
2. Open any world from any gamemode.  
3. Place an anvil, put any item into the anvil, open the anvil UI, and type a name that is exactly 18 characters long into the rename field.  
4. While the rename field is still active, hold **Shift** and press **Delete** to delete all text at once.  
5. Wait a moment for the game to process the input.  
6. Observe that the game crashes, showing a “Saving world” screen and producing a crash report.
Observed Behavior: When a player using Minecraft 1.14.3 opens an anvil and renames an item with a string that is exactly eighteen characters long, attempting to erase the entire name by holding Shift and pressing Delete causes the client to freeze on a “saving world” screen and then crash. The crash is triggered during the rendering of the anvil screen, specifically when the game tries to draw a button and calls String.substring with an invalid index, resulting in a java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException indicating a string index of –1. The stack trace shows the exception originating in java.lang.String.substring, followed by calls to cxa.renderButton, cws.render, dat.render, dko.a, cvo.e, cvo.b and finally net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main. The crash occurs on the client thread while the screen name is reported as “dat”, the mouse cursor is positioned at scaled coordinates (243, 82) corresponding to absolute coordinates (974.34, 328.14), the screen size is 480 × 270 scaled (1920 × 1080 absolute) and the GUI scale factor is 4.0. The affected level is the overworld on a non‑integrated multiplayer server named MpServer, with two players present, and the world seed is 0. All other world details such as chunk cache size, dimension, time, weather and game mode are recorded in the report, but the immediate cause of the crash is the out‑of‑bounds string operation during button rendering triggered by the Shift‑Delete action on an eighteen‑character name.
Expected Behavior: When a player places an item on an anvil, enters an 18‑character name and then presses Shift + Delete to erase the entire text, the text field should simply be cleared and the anvil GUI should close or remain open without throwing an exception, and the game should continue running normally without any crash or “saving world” message.
